title: Rome's integrity objection: Scripture's sincerity cannot be learned from Scripture alone
source_text: XXXV. Addunt adversarii, Necesse est ut sciamus non tantum Scripturae libros ex se divinos esse, dictatos a Spiritu sancto, sed etiam sinceros & incorruptos hodie reperiri, & tales ad nostras manus pervenisse. Id autem non possumus ex ipsa Scriptura discere: ac propterea opus est alio Dei verbo, per quod certi reddamur de Scripturae ipsius sinceritate & integritate. Sola ergo Scriptura non est fidei regula sufficiens.
pass_a_gloss: The adversaries add, It is necessary that we know not only that the books of Scripture are divine of themselves, dictated by the Holy Spirit, but also that they are found sincere and uncorrupted today, and have come such to our hands. But that we cannot learn from Scripture itself: and therefore there is need of another word of God, by which we may be made certain of the sincerity and integrity of Scripture itself. Therefore Scripture alone is not a sufficient rule of faith.
pass_b_english: Rome adds: we must know not only that Scripture's books are Spirit-dictated, but that they remain sincere and uncorrupted in our hands.
That integrity, they say, cannot be learned from Scripture itself — so another divine word seems required.
Hence their claim that Scripture alone is not a sufficient faith-rule.

choices.why: Textual integrity of the received books.
